summaryTab.matchCommentary:
The Test match at New Wanderers Stadium commenced with high tactical intensity as South Africa posted 426/10 (124.1 ov) in their opening innings. In response, Sri Lanka countered with 131/10 (45.4 ov), setting the stage for a compelling contest of tactical endurance. Early sessions tested batting resolve against disciplined seam movement, with both attacks striving to gain the upper hand on a developing surface.

The defining turning point arrived during 292-Run Stand: JP Duminy & HM Amla, which irrevocably altered the trajectory of the match. As the match progressed through its pivotal middle stages, JP Duminy delivered a masterclass for South Africa (155 Runs), absorbing intense pressure and tilting the momentum decisively. Crucial partnership stands and incisive bowling spells broke the opposition's resistance, shifting the control share (South Africa 64%) and allowing South Africa to dictate terms heading into the decisive sessions.

Entering the final innings, Sri Lanka faced an uphill battle under unrelenting scoreboard pressure. South Africa's bowling unit, bolstered by WD Parnell (23 Runs & 6 Wkts), maintained relentless discipline and attacked the stumps relentlessly. Wicket clusters in the closing sessions dismantled any remaining resistance, sealing South Africa won by innings & 118 runs in comprehensive fashion.

Verdict: South Africa's triumph was built on superior pressure absorption, clinical execution during critical moments, and the ability to dominate key sessions. While Sri Lanka produced fighting phases, South Africa won the pivotal turning points and sustained higher tactical control across all five days to emerge as deserved victors.
